request.spec:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the activity of the sheet: for every user and every event in the sheet's audit file, one
line <user> <EVENT> <count>, sorted by user then event.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has an Activity view: pressing **Show activity** lists one line `<user> <EVENT> <count>` for every user and event in the sheet's audit file, sorted by user then event. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the new activity test and the 3 other scenarios.

What changed:
- **Server:** `Audit.activity(sheetId)` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/Audit.java` reads the sheet's audit records and counts them per user and event. A new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit/activity` in `AuditController`, returns those lines.
- **Front end:** a new `app-activity` component in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/audit/activity.ts`, shown on the home screen beside the audit viewer, plus an `activity()` call in `audit-api.ts`.
  - It uses the test's `activity-show` button and `activity-line` items, and shows an `activity-error` message if the lines can't be read.
  - Pressing the button clears the old lines before showing the new ones, and loading a sheet resets the view.

The view only reads the audit file, so it adds no audit records of its own.
